newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid bourse seen reaching 500 points by summer.
newsitem.headline: Madrid bourse seen reaching 500 points by summer.

text.p: The Madrid bourse, just five months after vaulting the 400 point mark, is likely to soon surpass 500, bolstered by improving economic and corporate growth prospects, analysts said on Friday.
"This year we are going to see 500 points, probably before summer, said Valentin Fernandez, analyst at Credit Lyonnais.

The Madrid bourse, which took three years to go from 300 to 400, is near the 500 mark already, but is unlikely to manage the final stage until worries about a U.S. interest rate hike at the end of May have abated, analysts said.

On Friday, the index ended at a new high of 491.16, up 0.45 points, or 0.09 percent, helped higher by strength in Telefonica de Espana which was supporting the bourse after news of a key alliance with U.S.-based MCI and British Telecommunications.
The index ended Thursday at a new closing high of 490.71.

The macroeconomy has left behind the severe problems of the past, entering into what the government calls a circle of virtue, where declining inflation and deficit prompt interest rate declines which in turn boost economic activity.

"Inflation is clearly oriented downward, there are expectations for new declines in interest rates and growing possibilities that Spain will be in European Economic and Monetary Union," said Felix Gonzalez, director of economic analysis at Beta Capital.
Corporate profits are seen gaining ground from a reduction in salary expenses, lower financing costs and the recently agreed labour reform accord.
"The relation between lower interest rates and higher corporate earnings is seen clearly," said Antonio Garcia Rebollar, a managing director at Renta 4.
For Garcia Rebollar, the greater capacity for savings in all segments will necessarily favour equity markets.
"A rise in savings, in the context of declining interest rates, will help the bourse," he said

In addition, the bourse should benefit from changes in Spanish investment patterns, which are increasingly seeking out the higher returns of riskier investments now that interest rates have fallen amid European convergence.

"The behaviour of the Spanish investor has to converge more with international schemes and assume more risk to get more attractive yields," said Felix Gonzalez. "Institutions and individual investors have realised that there has been a change in the structure of Spanish interest rates."
Reinvigorated private consumption is also expected to bolster the bourse.
"Private consumption is driving forward," Fernandez said.
